messages.author: 01ee9baab3340811
messages.subject: compilation error with PF_RW sampler
parts:
Hi all nimble users!

I had an error at this statement,
cParticleMCMC <- compileNimble(Particleconf, project = cParticle_model, resetFunctions = TRUE)  
Compiling
  [Note] This may take a minute.
  [Note] Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compilation details.
Error in nimbleProject$instantiateCmodelValues(thisObj, dll) :
  Trying to instantiate a modelValues type that the project has no record of. Try setting option resetFunctions = TRUE in compileNimble

I guess this error can be related to PF_RW sampler because there is no error without this sampler. 
And I'm curious that this error message suggest use  "resetFunctions = TRUE", but I'm using.

How can I solve this error and what this error means?
I attach the script with full model.

Any advice and questions are welcome!

Thanks!
Kei

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: compilation error with PF_RW sampler
parts:
Hi Kei,

Thanks for reporting this (and for providing your input data files separately).

The issue here is that you have multiple particle filter (PF) samplers in the same MCMC. We hadn't tested that possibility, and there are some internal issues that prevent that from working in the current nimble. I'll be making a note for the developer team to consider modifications that would make this possible to do.

My suggestion for your work is that instead of having multiple PF samplers that you set up a single PF sampler on all of the top-level nodes (x,y,std2_1,std_r, and rho). Depending on the posterior dependence structure of the parameters, it could be that using a single PF sampler might mix better (or it might mix worse) than the three separate ones you wanted to use. It will definitely run faster because nimble will be running only one PF per MCMC iteration rather than three.

If you really want to use multiple PF samplers, we have an idea for a work-around that we could share. Let us know if so - it would probably take a few days for us to create the code for the work-around.

-Chris

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: compilation error with PF_RW sampler
parts:
Hi Kei,

Here is the work-around.

1) Run the code in the attached file first. This will set things up so that only one bootstrapFilter, called `bootstrapMultiple`, is created. That filter will get used for your three different samplers.
2) In your code, when you add the PF sampler, set `pfType = bootstrapMultiple`, so that the sampler uses the revised filter.

Since this is experimental, please check your results carefully to make sure they make sense.

-chris
